purpose: Take a coordinated snapshot of Qdrant (SocratiCode's backing store) and ai-memory, restore both into a fresh disposable prefix/ports, and verify each client, pointed explicitly at the disposable servers, returns query results consistent with the live originals.
preregistered: If (a) Qdrant collection snapshots restored into a fresh disposable Qdrant instance produce byte-identical point payloads and a SocratiCode process pointed at that instance reports the same indexed-chunk/file/edge counts as live and returns identical codebase_search results for a fixed query, and (b) an ai-memory backup restored into a fresh disposable data dir + a fresh disposable ai-memory server (new port) returns identical search results for a fixed query, while a marker written only to the disposable instance does not leak to the live instance, then coordinated cross-application snapshot/restore within one host is established for these two applications (supports_incumbent, scoped to same-host, synthetic-timing restore -- production/cross-host recovery and lost-key/account recovery remain explicitly out of scope per the gap text and are not claimed here).

result: A coordinated snapshot-and-restore of Qdrant (both the socraticode_metadata registry collection and the agent-lab codebase_72cfa87c5abf vector collection, 1242 points) into a fresh disposable Qdrant instance (port 36333, empty storage_path) produced byte-identical data (same point ids/payloads for the registry; same point count for the vectors) and, when a fresh SocratiCode process was pointed at it via QDRANT_URL alone, reported the identical indexed state (1242 chunks, 99 files, 73 edges) and returned a byte-for-byte identical codebase_search result (same 3 files, same scores, same order) compared with a query against the live, currently-running production instance. Separately, an ai-memory live-store backup (129 MiB tarball via the documented `ai-memory backup` command) was restored into a fresh disposable data dir and served from a new disposable server (port 49399); a fixed search query returned results identical to the live server (8/8 matching ranked results), and a marker page written only to the disposable instance was found there and confirmed absent from the live instance, proving genuine isolation rather than an accidental proxy to the live server. The documented `ai-memory restore` CLI subcommand refused to run because of a host-wide single-instance-process guard that fires even for a different --data-dir while the live server (pid 365) is running; since stopping the live server is forbidden by this session's binding rules, the functionally equivalent manual step (tar-extracting the same three paths the backup contains: wiki/, db/, config.toml) was used instead and is recorded as a deviation from the documented CLI path, not a different restore mechanism.

verdict_impact.explanation: This directly answers the part of the gap that was executable on this host: a coordinated, same-host snapshot/restore of Qdrant+SocratiCode and of ai-memory into a fresh disposable prefix, verified by consistent (here, identical) query results with each client explicitly pointed at the disposable server. It does not and cannot establish production recovery (this was synthetic timing -- the live stores were not corrupted or lost, only copied), atomic cross-application consistency (the two backups were taken sequentially, seconds apart, not via a single coordinated barrier/lock across both services, so a write landing between the two snapshot calls would not be captured atomically), or lost-key/account recovery, all of which the gap explicitly separates out and which remain unqualified, consistent with the gap's own text.

limitations: The two snapshots (Qdrant, ai-memory) were taken sequentially via two separate API/CLI calls, not through a single atomic cross-service barrier; a write racing between them would not be captured consistently. This is a synthetic-timing test of the restore mechanism, not a production-consistency guarantee.

`ai-memory restore` could not be exercised as documented because of its host-wide running-process guard interacting with the rule against touching the live server; a manual tar-extraction was substituted and is recorded as a deviation, not validated as identical to what `restore` itself does internally (e.g. any migration/validation steps `restore` might run were skipped).

Only two of SocratiCode's several Qdrant-backed collections for the agent-lab project were restored (socraticode_metadata and codebase_72cfa87c5abf); the code-graph (codegraph_*) and symgraph_* collections were not restored, so codebase_graph_* tools were not re-verified post-restore.

Production/cross-host restore, lost-key/lost-account recovery, and native Claude/Codex MCP client rebinding after a full restore were not tested, per the gap's own scope and this unit's binding rules (no second physical host available; no MCP client reconnection testing of running sessions permitted).

The disposable ai-memory server had to fetch a fresh copy of its local embedding model (~87 MB, all-MiniLM-L6-v2) since the model file is not part of the backup tarball; a restore on a host without network access to that model would need the model pre-seeded, which is a real operational note for this recovery path.
